title: Can you book a sushi chef for a dinner party in Dubai?
body_markdown:
Yes. You can book a sushi chef for a dinner party in Dubai, but confirm the chef’s sushi experience, the proposed menu and the facilities needed before agreeing to the booking. A private chef booking does not automatically include sushi preparation, waiting staff or tableware, so ask for a written proposal covering the complete evening.


**TL;DR**

- Booking a sushi chef for a dinner party in Dubai requires confirmation of specialist experience, menu and kitchen requirements.
- Choose seated service for a paced dinner or a live station when watching preparation matters.
- Confirm raw, cooked and vegetarian choices separately, alongside allergies and ingredient restrictions.
- myCHEF provides private dining and catering; ask specifically about a sushi-focused brief before committing.


## Can you book a sushi chef for a dinner party in Dubai?

Yes, but book against a specific brief rather than the description ‘Japanese food’. Sushi preparation, a Japanese-inspired dinner and a live sushi counter are different requests. Ask the provider to explain which experience the proposed chef can deliver.

Start with the date, Dubai location, guest count and preferred format. You can [contact myCHEF](https://www.mychef.ae/contact) to enquire about a dinner party and establish whether a sushi-focused menu can be accommodated. Treat that enquiry as a request for confirmation, not confirmation of a specialist booking.

Use this sequence before committing:

1. **Describe the evening.** State whether guests will sit together, circulate around a station or share platters.
2. **Check the chef’s relevant experience.** Ask about the sushi styles proposed and who will prepare them.
3. **Agree the menu and dietary approach.** Distinguish raw fish, cooked seafood, vegetarian dishes and any ingredient restrictions.
4. **Confirm the practical scope.** Record equipment, staffing, access, service timing and cleaning responsibilities.
5. **Approve the written proposal.** Make sure the final document matches the discussion, including any agreed substitutions.

**Book the sushi experience you want, not simply a chef with a broad cuisine label.** That distinction gives you a clearer basis for comparing proposals.

## Which sushi dinner format suits your party?

Choose the format before discussing individual rolls or garnishes. The service style determines where the chef works, how guests receive their food and how much attention the host needs to give the evening.

The formats below are planning options to discuss, not confirmed packages from any particular provider.

| Format | Best for | Main advantage | Main limitation | Confirm before booking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seated service | Hosts who want everyone dining together | Gives the meal a clear sequence | Requires coordinated plating and table service | Course order, serving staff and clearing |
| Live station | Guests who want to watch preparation | Makes preparation part of the gathering | Needs a suitable working area and a plan for queues | Counter position, guest access and replenishment |
| Sharing platters | Informal parties with flexible conversation | Lets guests choose from a shared selection | Makes dietary separation and portion allocation less straightforward | Platter contents, serving utensils and replenishment |

A seated dinner suits an evening built around conversation at the table. A live station suits a gathering where guests are comfortable moving around. Sharing platters keep the format informal, but you still need someone responsible for bringing food out and clearing used dishes.

**Choose seated service for a structured dinner; choose a live station when watching the chef is part of the plan.** Neither format removes the need to discuss kitchen access, dietary requirements or staffing.


![Comparison of seated sushi service, a live preparation station and sharing platters](https://media.get-ryze.ai/workspace-article-images-public/ffaab223-d0ef-4b42-bde2-0e5fed8d2610/body-4253bee7d3e9833901b2e3f93a4dd947.jpg)

*Choose the service format before finalising the menu.*


## What should you ask about the chef’s sushi experience?

Ask questions that connect the chef’s experience to your menu. A general cuisine description does not tell you whether the proposed chef regularly prepares the dishes you want or how those dishes will be served in your home.

Useful questions include:

- Which sushi styles would the chef propose for this setting?
- Which elements will be prepared before arrival, and which will be finished on site?
- Can the provider share an example menu relevant to this brief?
- How will the chef accommodate guests who do not eat raw fish?
- Who approves substitutions if an agreed ingredient changes?

Do not treat an example menu as your final menu. Ask for the agreed dishes to appear in the proposal, together with alternatives where needed. Photographs can help explain presentation, but they do not replace a clear description of portions and service.

**myCHEF is a relevant private dining option for hosts seeking a chef-led dinner at home.** Its stated services include vetted chefs and dinner parties; a sushi-specific enquiry still needs confirmation of the proposed chef and menu. Vetting and cuisine suitability answer different questions, so establish both.

## What should the sushi menu include?

Build the menu around what your guests will eat, rather than making raw fish the default. Ask each household about allergies, ingredient restrictions and preferences before the chef designs the meal.

A mixed group needs clearly described choices. ‘Vegetarian option available’ is less useful than knowing which dishes are vegetarian, how they will be served and whether they form a complete meal.

### An illustrative menu brief

The following is a planning example, not an advertised menu or a confirmed service:

- **Opening dishes:** a vegetable starter and a cooked dish for guests who prefer a warm beginning.
- **Sushi selection:** agreed raw-fish choices, cooked fillings and vegetable rolls, identified separately.
- **Additional main dish:** a cooked option for guests who do not want sushi as their whole meal.
- **Finish:** a dessert agreed around the group’s preferences and dietary requirements.

Ask the chef to explain the balance of the meal and the intended portions. A piece count alone does not describe how substantial the dinner will be: a small nigiri piece and a filled roll portion are not interchangeable planning units.

For an illustrative party of **8 guests**, your brief might identify **6 adults** and **2 children**. That breakdown is more useful than the total alone if the children need different dishes. It is not a portion recommendation; the chef should propose quantities against the agreed menu.

## How should you handle allergies and raw-fish preferences?

Separate allergies from preferences in your written brief. ‘Does not enjoy shellfish’ and ‘has a shellfish allergy’ require different conversations with the provider. Do not leave the distinction to a discussion at the dinner table.

Give the provider the ingredient concerned, the guest affected and any information the guest supplies about cross-contact. Ask whether the proposed kitchen setup and preparation process can meet that requirement. Do not assume that removing a garnish makes a dish suitable.

For guests avoiding raw seafood, ask for fully cooked or vegetarian dishes and confirm their preparation separately. Guests who are pregnant, immunocompromised or following medical dietary advice should follow their clinician’s guidance rather than rely on an event menu description.

If halal suitability matters, ask about the complete recipe, including sauces, seasonings and marinades. A Japanese dish name alone does not establish its ingredients. Get the agreed restrictions recorded alongside the menu so substitutions do not undermine the brief.

## What does your kitchen need for a sushi dinner?

Send the provider a practical description of the kitchen before the menu is finalised. Include photographs of the worktops, sink, refrigeration and cooking appliances if requested. Explain whether preparation will happen beside the dining area or in a separate kitchen.

Confirm these arrangements:

- **Preparation space:** identify the clear counter area available to the chef.
- **Refrigeration:** agree what storage is needed and what you must clear beforehand.
- **Equipment:** establish who supplies knives, boards, specialist tools and any cooking equipment.
- **Service ware:** confirm plates, platters, chopsticks, cutlery and serving utensils.
- **Access:** explain parking, building entry, service lifts and the route to the kitchen.
- **Waste and cleaning:** agree where waste goes and what the team will clean before leaving.

For a live station, guests need a viewing position that does not obstruct preparation or the route used by serving staff. Agree the layout with the provider rather than moving furniture after setup begins.

If you are unsure where household supplies end and the chef’s equipment begins, read the guide to [groceries and equipment for private chef visits](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/do-private-chefs-in-dubai-bring-their-own-groceries-and-equipment). Use it to prepare questions, then rely on your event’s written agreement for the actual scope.

## Why does a sushi dinner proposal vary?

Compare proposals against the same brief. A chef preparing food in the kitchen and a staffed dinner with table service are different scopes, even when the proposed dishes sound similar.

These factors change what the provider needs to deliver:

- **Guest count and portions:** include everyone eating, with separate notes for children or alternative meals.
- **Ingredient selection:** identify requested fish, cooked dishes and substitutions rather than relying on broad menu descriptions.
- **Preparation format:** distinguish work completed before arrival from preparation and finishing in your kitchen.
- **Staffing:** separate the chef’s responsibilities from serving, clearing and drinks service.
- **Equipment and tableware:** specify what your home provides and what the provider must bring.
- **Event schedule and access:** include arrival, setup, service, clearing and any building-entry arrangements.

Ask for inclusions and exclusions in the same document. If one proposal includes serving staff and another does not, resolve that difference before comparing the overall offer.

For a sushi dinner enquiry, myCHEF should receive the same detail you would send any other provider. That keeps the conversation focused on your event rather than assumptions about what a private chef booking normally includes.

## Do you need serving staff as well as a sushi chef?

You need to agree who handles every task outside food preparation. A chef working at a live counter is not automatically responsible for topping up drinks, clearing plates or managing guests’ requests across the room.

List the service tasks you want covered: setting the table, carrying dishes, explaining the menu, clearing between courses and washing up. Ask the provider to assign responsibility for each one. **Do not infer full table service from the phrase ‘private chef’.**

A host who wants to remain at the table needs a different arrangement from a host happy to carry platters and clear dishes. Neither choice is wrong; the proposal needs to reflect it.

## How far ahead should you enquire?

Enquire once you know the date, location and approximate guest count. Ask when the provider needs the final menu, dietary information and confirmed numbers rather than assuming a standard booking window.

Build the evening backwards from the intended serving time. The chef needs an agreed arrival and setup plan; you need to know when the kitchen must be clear. For Dubai apartments and managed villas, check any entry arrangements with the building or property contact before confirming access details.

Ask separately about the terms for date changes, guest-count changes and cancellation. Those terms belong in the booking agreement, not in an informal understanding about how the evening will work.

## FAQ


**Can I book a sushi chef for a dinner party in Dubai at home?**

Yes, you can arrange a sushi-focused dinner at home, subject to a provider confirming the chef, menu and practical requirements. Ask specifically about sushi experience rather than assuming it is included in every private chef service.

**Can a sushi dinner include food for guests who do not eat raw fish?**

Yes, a sushi dinner brief can request cooked and vegetarian dishes alongside raw-fish choices. Confirm the actual dishes, portions and preparation arrangements before approving the menu.

**Is a live sushi station better than a seated dinner?**

A live sushi station suits guests who want to watch preparation; seated service suits a paced meal at the table. Choose according to your space, guest preferences and desired level of table service.

**Does a sushi chef bring ingredients and equipment?**

Ingredients and equipment are booking-specific inclusions that you must confirm in writing. Ask separately about specialist tools, refrigeration, plates, serving utensils and anything your household must provide.

**Can a sushi chef cater for food allergies?**

Allergy suitability requires confirmation from the provider for the specific menu and preparation environment. Share the allergy before menu design and ask about ingredients, substitutions and cross-contact controls.

**Does booking a sushi chef include cleaning afterwards?**

Cleaning is included only to the extent stated in your agreement. Confirm whether the scope covers preparation surfaces, equipment, dishes, waste removal and the dining area.

**What should I send when requesting a sushi dinner proposal?**

Send the event date, Dubai location, guest count and preferred service format. Add dietary requirements, kitchen details, serving time and the staffing or tableware you want included.

Ask who will handle the table while the chef prepares the food. It is a small question with a direct effect on whether you spend the evening hosting your guests or carrying dishes.

Send myCHEF your **date, Dubai location, guest count and required service**. Specify that you want a sushi-focused dinner, describe your preferred format and include dietary requirements so the team can confirm suitability and prepare a relevant proposal.
